newsitem.title: UK: Mercury says new rules will aid pricing.
newsitem.headline: Mercury says new rules will aid pricing.

text.p: Mercury Communications Plc, part of the Cable and Wireless Plc group, welcomed regulatory changes announced by British industry watchdog OFTEL on Wednesday, saying they provided more flexibility on pricing.
"We are delighted. Under the new regime we can be more flexible in our prices. It increases our ability to be more competitive," a Mercury Communications official told Reuters.

OFTEL said it was proposing Mercury have a simplified license covering both domestic and international operations and a number of obligations be removed to reflect Mercury's non-dominant postion, particularly in the domestic market.
The Mercury official said this flexibility would close the gap with its much bigger rival British Telecommunications Plc as far as the marketing of services was concerned.
Mercury has 11.5 percent of the UK's domestic telecommunications market compared with BT's 80 percent share.

Mercury described the measures as "another milestone," saying it would now be able to "tailormake" its tariff rates for its corporate clients and aim for an increase in market share. Last summer, OFTEL did away with requirements for Mercury to announce a tariff change 28 days in advance, allowing it to announce and effect changes on the same day.
Mercury said the measures meant OFTEL recognized that BT was still the dominant force in the market.
